correctness.rationale: At a=-1 the phase exactly satisfies u_{n+1}=sin(u_n), while x_{n+1}=x_n+u_{n+1} and y_{n+1}=-x_n. If u_0 is a multiple of π then u_1=0 and the image lies on the fixed line. Otherwise 0<|u_1|≤1 and the sign s persists while |u_n| decreases to zero, since the only fixed magnitude of sine on [0,1] is zero. The reciprocal-square increment expands as 1/3+u_n²/15+O(u_n⁴). Averaging gives v_n/n→1/3 for v_n=u_n^{-2}; then summation gives v_n=n/3+O(log n), and inversion gives u_n²=3/n+O(log n/n²). Subtracting the increments of n/3+(log n)/5 leaves a summable O(log n/n²) series, proving a finite constant rather than just an asymptotic equivalent for the logarithm. Independently checked the local coefficients with python3 /workspace/branches/replay_3_5/expansion_checks.py; the accompanying .log records the result. For x_n, separate s sqrt(3/j) from each phase term in the exact sum. The phase errors are O(log j/j^{3/2}), with tail O(log n/sqrt(n)); the sum of j^{-1/2} minus 2sqrt(n) has a finite limit with tail O(n^{-1/2}), since the differences from the integrals over [j-1,j] are summable. This proves the asserted intercept and bound; y_n=u_n-x_n gives the opposite intercept. Divergence excludes all nonexceptional orbits from recurrence; points captured from outside the line never revisit a sufficiently small neighborhood. The map preserves any given invariant probability in the measure-theoretic sense even if not invertible; recurrence on a countable Euclidean base implies almost-everywhere point recurrence, hence concentration on the closed fixed line. Conversely the fixed line supports arbitrary invariant probabilities and only fixed points are periodic. These statements use exact real arithmetic; the archived floating-point diagnostic was inspected, not executed, and could not decide exact capture near rounded multiples of π or the infinite-time assertions.
